reason: Value/transfer lens: the gain is not real on unseen embryos, and the idea overstates its own power. (1) Accounting error. 6bba_05db0fb1 is one of the 10 x138 head stems AND a dummy twin, so its 3 divisions are counted twice. The splits.json divisions_per_video give 6bba 125 = bed 88 + 78 clean clips 17 + 10 head stems 20. So the maximum bed is 125 divisions (+42%), not 128. The honest, head-free bed is 105 (+19%): 61 of the 78 clean clips have 0 GT divisions and 17 have exactly 1. For a TP-count arc the standard error falls by only about 8% (1-sqrt(88/105)). (2) The dominant error is bias, not variance. DeepCenter is honest on 6bba, but it used 6bba as its validation set (checkpoint selection, browser_intel s6.1 item 2). More importantly, the fork candidates come from the detector, edge net and seed314159, which were all trained on the 199 train clips (discussion 742064). The positions come from the V1284 head. The lab flatters candidate geometry on every train clip, which is the same trap as the edge filter (+0.016 in the lab, 0 on the LB). Adding more 6bba clips does not reduce this bias. (3) Prior public evidence on the same knob: sjlee101's forks of the 0.947 stack scored 0.946 / 0.947 / 0.947 at DeepCenter safe-div thresholds 0.15 / 0.20 / 0.25 (CONTEXT.md l.698-704). The public arc is flat to within 0.001. So K3b is unlikely ever to show the R4 +0.002, and the arc's realistic value is 0..+0.001. (4) Metric ceiling: score = adj_edge + 0.1*div_J, micro-averaged. K3b keeps the node set, so there is no node-multiplier term, and each fork adds one edge (a negligible edge-J effect). On the bed, one net TP flip is about +0.0008. The extension changes the decision only when the 39-clip bed passes (P ~0.3) and the pooled bed then disagrees (~0.2-0.3). The veto's saving is also limited to the case the LB gate would not catch (~0.15 x 0.0015). Expected value of information is about 1-2e-5. K3b is also meant as an F2 variance option, and the final score is max(F1,F2). A false pass there costs little, while a false veto (noise from only 17 honest divisions) removes an upside option. The net VOI is ~0, not the claimed +0.0001..+0.0003. The one genuine merit: exp60's bed was picked 'most divisions first' (30% of the 6bba clips hold 70% of the divisions), which over-weights TP opportunities and biases t* toward a permissive value. Only the zero-division clips reveal fork FPs at population density. That argues for a conditional veto check, not for 3 unconditional shards.
fix: Do not run the extension unconditionally. Run it lazily. Only if the pre-registered 39-clip 6bba bed passes the full E5 gate, push the 78 clean clips (2 shards, ~4 GPU-h) from the fresh quota and pool them with the bed at population weight. Use them only as a veto on the precision of the marginal forks and on the sign of the arc, and write this rule down before the E5 result is read. Fix the accounting in split_ext.json: 105 honest divisions; 05db0fb1 counts once, inside the head stems. Exclude the 10 head stems entirely rather than reporting them separately. Keep K3b in the F2 variance role only, given the flat public arc of sjlee101's 0.15/0.20/0.25 forks. If the 39-clip bed fails E5 (P ~0.7), spend nothing.
realistic_gain: ~0 on private (value of information <= ~2e-5). The underlying K3b arc is realistically 0..+0.001 given the flat public arc from 0.15 to 0.25. As a conditional veto it may save one S5 slot with P ~0.07.
